title: Public Citizen files FCC and FTC complaints over government-paid Trump ads
description_short: Public Citizen files FCC and FTC complaints over government-paid Trump ads
description_medium: Public Citizen asked the FCC and FTC to investigate broadcasters airing government-paid pro-Trump commercials and urged stations to stop carrying them. Its September 29 filing argues the spots are campaign advertising paid for with taxpayer funds. Reuters also reported the complaints. The filing raises allegations for regulators to examine; it is not an agency finding.
description_long: On September 29, 2026, Public Citizen filed complaints with the Federal Communications Commission and Federal Trade Commission about broadcasters airing government-paid commercials supporting President Donald Trump. The organization asked both agencies to investigate and urged stations to stop carrying the spots. In its submission, Public Citizen argued that the commercials functioned as campaign advertising and challenged the use of taxpayer money to pay for them. The group's ethics expert Craig Holman was identified in the supplied record. Reuters independently reported the complaints, confirming the filing as a new regulatory action. The distinction between an allegation and a finding is important: Public Citizen asked regulators to examine the broadcasts, but the supplied sources report no completed agency investigation or determination that the ads violated the law. The immediate event was therefore the filing and request for review, not an enforcement decision against a broadcaster. Any later agency response or station decision would be a separate development. The record also distinguishes this complaint from a separate September 25 filing to other government offices about the ads.
notes: The Public Citizen complaint is an allegation and request for investigation, not a regulatory finding. The event is distinct from the September 25 GAO/OSC complaint.
